items.bewering: Roer 'n lepel sout in 'n glas water en kyk hoe die korrels verdwyn. Die water bly helder maar proe nou sout. Die sout is dus nog in die water.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Solution' (britannica.com/science/solution-chemistry): salt water is the standard example of a homogeneous liquid solution; dissolved salt stays in the water and gives it its taste.

items.bewering: Ons noem die sout die opgeloste stof en die water die oplosmiddel.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Liquid - Solutions and solubilities': the liquid is customarily the solvent and the substance added the solute.

items.bewering: In water is die deeltjies naby aan mekaar in geen vaste patroon nie, en hulle beweeg by mekaar verby.
items.bron: American Chemical Society, Middle School Chemistry lesson 1.4 and CK-12 kinetic molecular theory: in a liquid particles are close together, not in a regular arrangement, and slide past each other.

items.bewering: Een soutkorrel bestaan uit ontelbaar baie deeltjies wat elkeen op 'n vaste plek bly.
items.bron: ACS Middle School Chemistry lesson 1.4: particles in a solid vibrate in fixed positions and do not move past one another; Britannica 'Crystal': a crystal is a regular lattice of atoms/ions. At particle-model level 'op 'n vaste plek' is the accepted description.

items.bewering: In die water raak die deeltjies aan die buitekant van die korrel los. Hulle gaan uitmekaar en meng eweredig tussen die waterdeeltjies in.
items.bron: Britannica 'Solution': a solution is homogeneous on the molecular scale; dissolution proceeds from the exposed surface of the solid.

items.bewering: Elke deeltjie is selfs met 'n vergrootglas te klein om te sien. Daarom bly die oplossing helder en hou elke druppel ewe veel sout.
items.bron: Dissolved ions are about 0.1-1 nm across (Wikipedia 'Filter paper' context and general chemistry references), far below what a magnifying glass resolves; Britannica 'Solution': composition at any point is the same as at any other.

items.bewering: Die soutdeeltjies is baie kleiner as die gaatjies in 'n sif of 'n filter. Hulle loop saam met die water deur en wat onder uitdrup, proe steeds sout.
items.bron: True for a sieve and for filter paper (pores roughly 2-25 micrometres against dissolved ions of about 0.1-1 nm; Wikipedia 'Filter paper'). False as a claim about 'a filter' in general: reverse-osmosis membranes are filters whose pores (about 1-5 angstrom) hold back dissolved salt, and they are how seawater desalination plants, including South African ones, remove salt (Yale Engineering news on reverse osmosis; membrane literature, e.g. PMC13120458). The block heading 'Waarom 'n filter nie help nie' repeats the general form. A learner who hears about desalination will find the lesson's rule broken.
items.regstelling: Beperk die bewering tot die filter wat die leerder ken, sonder om die res van die blok te verander: bv. 'Die soutdeeltjies is baie kleiner as die gaatjies in 'n sif of in filtreerpapier.' Die kop kan ook na die skoolfilter verwys (bv. 'Waarom filtreerpapier nie help nie'). Moenie beweer dat geen filter ooit sout kan uithaal nie.

items.bewering: Met die hand sorteer werk ook nie, want daar is geen stukkies om uit te haal nie.
items.bron: Follows from the particle size above (ions far below visible size); CK-12 'Wet methods of separation': dissolved solids cannot be picked or filtered out.

items.bewering: Soutwater in 'n toe bottel bly helder al staan dit lank. Uitsakking en oorgiet help dus ook nie, want niks sak na die bodem nie.
items.bron: Britannica 'Solution': a true solution is homogeneous at the molecular scale and does not separate on standing; the closed bottle rules out evaporation.

items.bewering: Tog kan jy die opgeloste stof uit sommige oplossings herwin deur die oplosmiddel te laat verdamp.
items.bron: EU Salt, 'Harvesting salt by solar evaporation'; Britannica 'Salt manufacture'. 'Sommige' correctly avoids claiming every solute survives evaporation.

items.bewering: Herwin beteken hier terugkry, nie om afval weer te gebruik nie.
items.bron: Word meaning: Afrikaans 'herwin' carries both 'regain/recover' and 'recycle'; the lesson states which sense it uses. No factual risk.

items.bewering: Die water in soutwater verdamp stadig en gaan as waterdamp in die lug in. Die sout verdamp nie saam nie en bly agter. Dit is die water wat weggaan, nie die sout nie.
items.bron: EU Salt 'Harvesting salt by solar evaporation' and Morton Salt 'Salt production and processing': water evaporates and the salt precipitates and remains.

items.bewering: Seewater is 'n oplossing met baie sout daarin. Sommige sout word uit seewater gemaak.
items.bron: Britannica 'Salt manufacture'; Morton Salt: solar sea salt is one of several production routes (others are rock-salt mining and inland brines), so 'sommige' is accurate.

items.bewering: Mense laat seewater in groot vlak damme loop waar die son en die wind die water stadig laat verdamp. Die water kook nooit nie.
items.bron: EU Salt: seawater evaporates in open basins by the action of sun and wind; Morton Salt: large shallow ponds; US patent 4564367: the process runs at ambient temperature.

items.bewering: Ná 'n tyd lê daar 'n laag sout op die bodem, onder die soutwater wat oorbly.
items.bron: US patent 4564367 (Solar salt crystallizer): saturated brine is kept as a layer overlying the salt crop on the bottom of the crystallizer pond.

items.bewering: Gooi lepel ná lepel suiker in 'n glas water en roer elke keer. Eers los elke lepel heeltemal op. Later bly daar suiker op die bodem lê, hoe lank jy ook al roer. Die oplossing is nou versadig. Daardie hoeveelheid water kan niks meer van die suiker oplos nie.
items.bron: CK-12 'Saturation': a saturated solution holds the maximum solute at that temperature and further solute stays undissolved. The glass setting implies constant temperature; the begrip entry states the temperature condition.

items.bewering: Suiker wat net nog nie opgelos het nie, maak die oplossing nog nie versadig nie.
items.bron: CK-12 'Saturation': saturation is defined by the solution's capacity, not by visible undissolved solid that is still dissolving.

items.bewering: 'n Sekere hoeveelheid water kan net 'n sekere hoeveelheid suiker opgelos hou. ... Gooi nou genoeg water by en roer weer. Dan los die suiker op die bodem ook op. Meer water kan dus meer suiker oplos.
items.bron: Solubility is a ratio (about 200 g sugar per 100 g water at 20 C; homework.study.com / ausetute solubility table), so more water dissolves proportionally more solute.

items.bewering: Sout en suiker het ook elkeen sy eie grens. Dieselfde glas water kan baie meer suiker as sout oplos.
items.bron: Sucrose about 200 g/100 g water at 20 C against sodium chloride about 36 g/100 mL (AUS-e-TUTE solubility table): roughly five to six times as much sugar by mass, so 'baie meer' holds.

items.bewering: Soos soutwater verdamp, raak die water later te min om al die sout opgelos te hou. Die ekstra sout kom dan uit die oplossing as klein harde kristalle. Ons noem dit kristallisasie.
items.bron: EU Salt: brine evaporates up to the saturation point, then salt precipitates; US patent 4564367: sodium chloride crystals recovered in the crystallizer. Britannica 'Crystal'.

items.bewering: 'n Helder soutoplossing staan in 'n vlak bak. / Die water verdamp stadig en word al hoe minder. / Klein soutkristalle verskyn in die bak en word groter. / Uiteindelik is al die water weg en net droë sout bly oor.
items.bron: Same sources as the crystallisation block (EU Salt; Britannica 'Crystal' on crystal growth). For a solution of table salt in water, full evaporation leaves only the salt.

items.bewering: opgeloste stof: Die stof wat in 'n vloeistof opgelos het, soos die sout in soutwater.
items.bron: Britannica 'Liquid - Solutions and solubilities': the substance added is the solute. Liquid-only framing is a grade-level narrowing, not a falsehood.

items.bewering: oplosmiddel: Die vloeistof waarin 'n stof oplos, soos die water in soutwater.
items.bron: Britannica 'Liquid - Solutions and solubilities': the liquid in a solution is customarily designated the solvent.

items.bewering: versadigde oplossing: 'n Oplossing waarin daardie hoeveelheid water by daardie warmte niks meer van die stof kan oplos nie.
items.bron: CK-12 'Saturation': a saturated solution contains the maximum amount of solute that dissolves at a given temperature. The entry is water-specific, which matches the lesson's examples.

items.bewering: kristal: 'n Vaste stof waarin die deeltjies in 'n netjiese, herhalende patroon gerangskik is.
items.bron: Britannica 'Crystal'; LibreTexts 'Crystalline and amorphous solids': atoms, ions or molecules in a highly ordered repeating three-dimensional pattern.

items.bewering: kristallisasie: Wanneer 'n opgeloste stof as kristalle uit 'n oplossing kom.
items.bron: Britannica 'Crystal' (crystal growth from solution); EU Salt solar evaporation. Crystallisation also occurs from melts and vapours, but as a description of crystallisation from a solution the entry is correct.

items.bewering: verdamp: Wanneer 'n vloeistof in 'n gas verander. Dit gebeur vinniger wanneer die vloeistof warmer is.
items.bron: Chemistry LibreTexts 13.2 'Evaporation and condensation': evaporation is liquid to gas at the surface, and the rate rises with temperature.

items.bewering: waterdamp: Water in die vorm van 'n gas wat niemand kan sien nie.
items.bron: Energy Education 'Water vapour' and Wikipedia 'Steam': water vapour is invisible; the visible 'steam' from a kettle and clouds are condensed liquid droplets.

items.bewering: oplossing: 'n Mengsel waarin een of meer stowwe in 'n vloeistof opgelos het. Dit lyk oral dieselfde.
items.bron: Britannica 'Solution': a homogeneous mixture, same composition at every point; the word is 'commonly applied to the liquid state', though solid (alloys) and gaseous (air) solutions exist. The liquid framing is a grade-level narrowing that does not assert that only liquids form solutions; noted so a later grade can widen it.

items.bewering: oplos: Wanneer die deeltjies van 'n stof losraak en tussen die deeltjies van 'n vloeistof meng, sodat jy geen korrels meer kan sien nie.
items.bron: Britannica 'Solution': dissolution disperses the solute on the molecular scale among the solvent particles; ACS Middle School Chemistry chapter 5 (dissolving) describes the same particle picture.

items.bewering: deeltjie: Een van die piepklein stukkies waaruit alle materie bestaan. Dit is te klein om selfs met 'n vergrootglas te sien.
items.bron: ACS Inquiry in Action 'Matter is made of tiny particles': all matter is made of particles too small to see; ions and molecules are on the order of 0.1-1 nm, far beyond a magnifying glass.

opsomming: One claim is false as written: the lesson says salt particles are much smaller than the holes in 'a filter', but reverse-osmosis filters in desalination plants do remove dissolved salt, so the sentence and its heading must be narrowed to a sieve and filter paper; everything else, including the sugar-versus-salt solubility comparison and the sea-salt ponds, checks out, and the lesson contains no superlatives or analogy blocks.
